record_verbatim.evidence: Validator finding verbatim: 'safety requirement FB2-SAF-FSR-000004 has no fault_reaction defined'. Confirmed by direct inspection: the key 'fault_reaction' is absent from the whole document of FB2-SAF-FSR-000004 in profile synthetic_reference, so the rule's condition is exactly met. The requirement text is (independent ASIL B hardware monitor within 50 ms), and it states the detection or actuation bound in prose inside 'statement' rather than in a structured field. A corpus-wide recursive check found the key absent from all seven FSR instances across both profiles.
record_verbatim.impact: The corpus holds no machine-readable record of what the system must DO on detection of any of its safety faults: no reaction time, no reaction target, and no degraded-mode statement per requirement. The information exists only as prose. That has a concrete consequence beyond tidiness: a checker cannot compare a stated reaction time against a requirement, which is precisely how an incorrect timing claim survived into the safety case. FB2-SAF-SCS-000001 asserts a 70 ms chain that is both arithmetically wrong and inconsistent with the requirements it cites, and with no structured reaction-time field there is nothing for a validator to contradict it with.

record_verbatim.resolution:
RESOLVED. The condition this record detected was real: the safety-requirement completeness rule (MUT-008, safety_requirement_completeness_checker) requires a machine-readable fault_reaction on every safety-domain requirement, and at the time this record was raised FB2-SAF-FSR-000004 in profile synthetic_reference had none. The reaction existed only as prose inside `statement`, which is why a checker could not compare a stated reaction time against a requirement - the concrete harm this record's impact field named.

WHAT FIXED IT: a populated `fault_reaction` object authored onto FB2-SAF-FSR-000004 at revision 3, recorded in that record's own revision_history. For the synthetic_reference copies the block is a full allocation - allocated_element_id, element_owns_reaction, reaction, triggered_by, reaction_time_budget_ms, mode_dependence, allocation_basis and open_limits - traced to the element FB2-SAF-FSC-000001 allocates the reaction to. For the as_is copies it is the honest answer instead: those records have origin source_observed, so the reaction is copied from the observed source rather than from the synthetic concept, and where the element owns no reaction the block says so and says why. That asymmetry is the point of the block and is why it was worth authoring rather than suppressing.

EVIDENCE, re-derived on 2026-09-30T00:00:00Z: FB2-SAF-FSR-000004 in profile synthetic_reference carries a populated fault_reaction object with fields ['allocated_element_id', 'allocation_basis', 'element_owns_reaction', 'mode_dependence', 'open_limits', 'reaction', 'reaction_time_budget_ms', 'triggered_by']. The rule is silent on it. The rule was NOT weakened to achieve this and no requirement was reclassified to dodge it - the opposite happened, see below.

THE RULE ALSO GOT WIDER WHILE THIS WAS BEING FIXED, and that is the part this record could not have known. MUT-008 used to carry a third condition, `"-FSR-" in id`, which made it structurally incapable of reporting the five FB2-SAF-SEC-* security requirements - a different class of safety-domain requirement, carrying the whole cybersecurity concept, which this rule was always meant to cover. The filter has been removed; the rule's scope was widened and nothing was narrowed. Four self-tests now pin that widened scope from both sides. Recorded as FB2-REV-FND-000039. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false. No human approved this revision, no tool is claimed to be qualified, and no certification, ISO 26262 conformity or ASPICE capability level is claimed or implied.

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/<profile>/<id>.json, then record the approval as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block on the record, plus approval_ledger_ref naming one appended line in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. Do NOT add a revision_history entry: see docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.
